full_judgment: The opposite parties as plaintiff instituted a suit for specific performance of contract with a prayer for execution and registration of the kabala in respect of the suit land by the defendant No. 1 and, in default, by the court in their favour stating that the suit land comprising 0.49 acres out of 0.88 acres of land of the SA Plot No. 294 corresponding to CS Plot No. 735 appertaining to SA Khatian No. 14 and CS Khatian No. 35 is owned by the defendant No 1. The defendant No. 1 wanted to purchase land at the village Bangola and as such he was in need of money. Consequently he proposed to the plaintiffs for selling the suit land in the first part of Falgoon 1384 BS. As the plaintiffs earlier purchased some lands in the suit plot, so they agreed to purchase the suit property also from the defendant No. 1. Accordingly, in pursuance of a talk between them the price of the suit property was fixed at Taka 10,000/-. Thereafter the plaintiff paid the earnest money amounting to Taka 8,000/- in four installments within the month of Falgoon 1384 BS. On receipt of the aforesaid amount of earnest money the defendant No. 1 handed over possession in respect of the cultivable portion of the suit land to the plaintiff. It was settled that the defendant No. 1 on receipt of the balance of the consideration amount within Aswin 1385 BS. would execute and register a regular deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff and then would deliver the homestead portion of the suit property in pursuance of the agreement. The plaintiff demanded kabala offering the balance of the consideration to the defendant No. 1 who avoided it on different pretexts. As the defendant No. 1 has not got possession of the purchased land in mouza Bangola he gave expression that he would not sell the suit land in spite of the contract.
